public_rationale: The verified scholarly record contains both criticism and continuing endorsement of the Turing Test. It does not establish a June 2022 field-wide wish to abandon it, or the prevalence of views about its significance. A literal unanimity reading faces documented dissent, but that alone does not settle the fairer reading as a broad-consensus claim.
limitations: The usable scholarly overview predates the target period.
Criticism of the test's limitations is not equivalent to believing it has no value.
Later Turing-test research was not used to infer earlier community attitudes.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The AI community wishes the Turing Test would go away, and its members all know that beating the test is not meaningful.
conditions: the AI community, as opposed to the public

statement.excerpt: The public knows the test of course, but the AI community wishes it would go away; we all know that beating that test isn’t meaningful.

from_speaker: the AI community wishes it would go away
our_interpretation: The test is the conversational Turing Test discussed in the surrounding passage.
Read 'we all' as a claim of broad field consensus, rather than a literal claim about every individual.
Meaningful refers to passing the test as a measure of AI progress. The claim also asserts a community preference to abandon it.
Use June 1 through June 12, 2022, for the ongoing community attitude described at publication.
The reference to the AI community rather than the public specifies the population; it is not a conditional forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Representative evidence establishes both broad rejection of passing the conversational Turing Test as meaningful evidence of AI progress and a broad preference to abandon it.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence establishes a substantial active constituency in the AI community that assigns the test meaningful value or wants to retain it. Isolated disagreement does not alone disprove the ordinary consensus reading.
